source_row.wylie: [iv.301-11a] ,gsum pa ni, phra ma ni bsams bzhin du ma nor bar pha rol po mdza' ba dbye ba'i phyir nyon mongs pa can gyi sems kyi tshig don pha rol pos go ba'o
source_row.english: Divisive speech consists of words which are spoken purposely, without any mistake, and in a mentally afflicted state; they are meant to split up others who are friends, and their meaning should be understood by the other person.

spans.nul: The complete ordinal is the third outline point. The entire English starts directly with Divisive speech and contains no number, ordinal, next/now transition or other exponent of third. This is affirmative absence of the outline label, not an uncertainty null; NI is separately omitted.

The error sense is mistake here, not mistaken identity from353. BAR completes adverbial grammar and is not mapped to between.
This first other-person expression names the people being divided. It is distinct from the later recipient who understands the words.
The complete friendship adjective/noun is rendered friends; exclude who are. The full glossary supports friends without correcting the source.
Dividing/separating verb owns the complete phrasal verb split up, excluding to, which belongs to the purpose relation.
Purpose particle gives meant to in this purpose construction. Exclude they are; do not turn BSAMS/purposely into this second purpose expression.

The understanding verb owns understood in the passive English. Should be remains outside; the attached declarative ending is not split.
